manual:
**Game plan:** grind card advantage with cheap removal and Flip recursion, then close with one protected beater. [YP-GOAT]

**Key cards / engine:** Scapegoat + Metamorphosis → Thousand-Eyes Restrict; Tsukuyomi + Magician of Faith/Dekoichi; Book of Moon; BLS.

**How to pilot / combo lines:**
- **The TER swing is two turns, not one.** Scapegoat is a Quick-Play; its text says "You cannot Summon other monsters the turn you activate this card" [CDB], so you cannot Scapegoat and Metamorphosis a token on the same turn. Make goats on the *opponent's* End Phase (or a prior turn), then on *your* turn tribute one token to `Metamorphosis` → `Thousand-Eyes Restrict`, which absorbs their best monster and locks the board [CDB].
- **Tsukuyomi is the value engine.** Flip your `Magician of Faith` face-down to re-use its flip (rebuy a Limited Spell), flip `Dekoichi` for another draw, or flip an opponent's face-up beater face-down — stripping its Equip and position and setting it up for `Nobleman of Crossout` or a clean attack. Tsukuyomi bounces to hand each End Phase [CDB], so it repeats.
- **Book of Moon** is your Swiss-army trick: flip your monster face-down to dodge targeted removal or a battle, flip the opponent's attacker mid-combat to blank it, deny a Tribute Summon, or flip a monster to enable `Nobleman of Crossout` [CDB].
- **Sequencing:** lead with floaters (`Sangan`, `Sinister Serpent`) and set one reactive trap; make the opponent commit into `Bottomless`/`Sakuretsu`/`Mirror Force`. Hold `Delinquent Duo` and `Graceful Charity` for when they refill your grip rather than emptying it.
- **Closing:** bank chip damage, then drop `Black Luster Soldier`; banish their wall (no attack that turn) or swing and take the double attack for lethal [CDB]. `Cyber-Stein → Master of Oz` is an emergency finisher, not the plan.

**Weaknesses:** soft to a fast `Heavy Storm` blowing out a set-heavy board, to being out-tempoed by pure aggro before the grind starts, and to your own brick hands (all traps / all monsters). Watch LP vs `Ring of Destruction`.

=== EXTRA DECK ===

**Read this as a list of *Levels*, not monsters.** Two doors only: `Metamorphosis` — "Tribute 1 monster. Special Summon 1 Fusion Monster from your Extra Deck with the same Level as the Tributed monster" [CDB], and `Cyber-Stein`. There is no `Polymerization` in the list and `Magical Scientist` is **Forbidden** in GOAT [GF-BAN], so nothing here is ever Fusion Summoned normally. Tokens are legal material ("including a Sheep Token from `Scapegoat`"), Metamorphosis "cannot be activated" if no Fusion in the list matches the tributed monster's Level, and it "does not properly Summon a Fusion Monster, so you cannot use `Monster Reborn` on it afterwards" [GR].

**Your fodder, by Level — Lv1:** Sheep Token, `Sinister Serpent`, `Magician of Faith`. **Lv5:** `Airknight Parshath`. **Lv6:** `Chaos Sorcerer`. **Lv9:** nothing — `Cyber-Stein` is the only door.

- **`Thousand-Eyes Restrict` (Lv1) — the format's signature card:** "the most frequent and most powerful fusion monster special summoned with Metamorphosis … it can take the opponent's best monster while locking down the field at the same time" [GF-FUS]. Make the goats in the opponent's End Phase [GW], convert a token on your turn, then **absorb with priority** — in GOAT rules "when a Chain or Summon has finished resolving, the turn player can activate a fast effect *or a monster's Ignition Effect* before the opponent is allowed to respond" [GF-BASICS], so equip the instant Metamorphosis resolves, before `Book of Moon` can land; if they flip it down first, TER "needs to be face up on the field to attach a monster to itself, so its effect will fizzle" [GR]. Then grind it: "when combined with Tsukuyomi, Restrict can take full control of the board and chip in for damage until the game is won" [GF-GOAT] — flip TER face-down and back up for a second absorb. Also, monsters equipped to TER "do not have effects and are treated as Equip Spell Cards" [GR], so it blanks what it steals.
- **`Dark Balter the Terrible` (Lv5) off a spent `Airknight Parshath`** [GW] — "after Thousand-Eyes Restrict, this is the most commonly used fusion monster brought forth with Metamorphosis … the potential to negate both spells and monster effects is quite powerful" [GF-FUS]: it pays 1000 LP to negate a Normal Spell (`Pot of Greed`, `Graceful Charity`, `Heavy Storm`, `Nobleman of Crossout`) and negates the effect of any Effect Monster it kills in battle [CDB]. Convert Airknight once it has stopped drawing you cards.
- **`Ryu Senshi` (Lv6) off `Chaos Sorcerer` — a kill-turn card**, "the most commonly used level 6 fusion monster, and it [is] mostly used for setting up kill turns via Chaos Sorcerer+Metamorphosis" [GF-FUS]. Sorcerer "cannot attack the turn you activate this effect" [CDB], so on the turn you banish with it, trade the idle body for a 2000 attacker: it pays 1000 LP to negate a **Normal Trap** (`Mirror Force`, `Torrential Tribute`, `Sakuretsu Armor`, `Ring of Destruction` — *not* the Counter Trap `Solemn Judgment`) and "negate[s] the effects of any Spell Card that targets this card and destroy[s] it" [CDB], walking through `Book of Moon` and `Snatch Steal`.
- **`Master of Oz` (Lv9) — `Cyber-Stein` only:** "With 4200 attack and 3700 defense, this has the best stats of any fusion monster in Goat Format. You won't be summoning it with Metamorphosis too often, but it is a common Cyber-Stein target" [GF-FUS]. No Level 9 body exists here, so Stein is its *only* door, and with no `Megamorph` in this list 5000 LP buys a plain 4200 beater — emergency finisher, not a plan.
- **`Musician King` (Lv5) — the LIGHT slot, for Chaos, not for combat.** You never make a 1750 vanilla for its body. The sourced job of a LIGHT Level-5 Fusion is graveyard fuel: "in the rare situations where you have `Snatch Steal` for your opponent's `Airknight Parshath` and need to Metamorphosis for a light monster in your graveyard for a chaos monster [it] could be the difference between winning and losing the game" [GF-FUS]. The mechanism matters: a monster you took with `Snatch Steal` goes back to *their* Graveyard when you tribute it, so the LIGHT you actually bank is the Fusion itself once it dies — re-arming `Chaos Sorcerer`/`BLS`, which each need "1 LIGHT and 1 DARK" banished [CDB]. That guide picks `Giltia the D. Knight` (also LIGHT, Level 5, 1850 ATK) for this slot and never names Musician King — same job, 100 more ATK.
- **`Flame Swordsman` (Lv5) — ⚠ unverified line.** FIRE 1800 vanilla. GoatFormat.com's level-by-level guide ranks the Level-5 fusions as `Dark Balter the Terrible`, `Fiend Skull Dragon`, `Reaper on the Nightmare` and `Giltia the D. Knight`, and **never mentions Flame Swordsman** [GF-FUS]; I found no source giving it a role. Real GOAT puts no size cap on the fusion deck [GF-FUS], which is why lists carry redundant Levels — treat this as a spare Level-5 body for after the first one has been destroyed, and nothing more.
